extracted.intended_audience: educators, instructional designers, and researchers in distance and higher education
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluation dimensions for designing, implementing, and assessing mobile (m-)learning in higher education and distance education contexts. Includes pedagogical, technical, accessibility, and evaluation considerations drawn from practice and pilot studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility (remove barriers; anytime/anywhere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing barriers to enable learning anytime, anywhere for learners worldwide and increasing the equality of educational opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include mobile-friendly library resources (DRR), MP3 audio versions of readings, low-/high-speed streaming options, and TTS audio. Accessibility was measured in pilots (e.g., 90% agreed mobile tech provided flexibility). Consider credentialing and how accessibility interacts with quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner control and flexibility (cafeteria-style choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for learner-centred, cafeteria-style educational choices where learners control what, when, and how they learn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for self-selection, modular lessons, and on-demand content. Consider implications for assessing quality and credentialing when learners pick discrete items rather than following linear courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portability and device-appropriate content
rubrics_metrics.description: Portability of mobile devices as an affordance for learning (learn 'in-your-pocket' and 'on-the-fly').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide content appropriate to brief, mobile contexts (MP3 clips, short exercises). Use formats and sizes suitable for phones, PDAs, and MP3 players to leverage portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactivity, meaningfulness, and learner-centred design
rubrics_metrics.description: Next-generation learning environments should be 'highly interactive, meaningful, and learner-centred.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for cognitive authenticity and tasks that reflect real domain activity. Use collaborative/social features (learning swarms) and design that engages the Net Generation's preference for doing and interactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-in-time learning and immediacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for 'just-in-time' learning — delivering the right content at the right moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure small, focused learning objects and quick-reference materials. Ensure fast access and low-latency delivery where immediacy matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for learners with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of formats and technologies that increase access for learners with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MP3 audio, text-to-speech, and alternative format provision. IRRODL and DRR MP3 offerings and TTS conversions are examples that improve accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform compatibility and device heterogeneity handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to handle lack of a common platform among manufacturers and device types (smartphones, cellphones, PDAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement auto-detection and device-specific formatting (e.g., WAP, JSP reformatting in AirPac). Provide fallbacks and multiple output formats to accommodate heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability constraints of mobile hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize central disadvantages such as small display screens, reduced storage capacity, and reliance on battery power; also eyesight issues for older learners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dense text and complex activities on small screens; design short interactions; provide printable/downloadable PDFs or alternative desktop views for heavy reading tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security and network/bandwidth concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Security issues inherent in using wireless devices and the impact of network load on bandwidth and immediacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for secure connections, manage DRM appropriately, and provide low-bandwidth alternatives (low-speed streams) where network limits exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional design principle: introduce new tech in familiar contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce new technologies in a familiar context; adapt pedagogy to match learners' existing contexts and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: mobile ESL used familiar grammar lessons repackaged for phones. Use familiar content/format metaphors to reduce cognitive load when introducing mobile modalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptivity to learner characteristics and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt functionality for learner characteristics and learning context (personalization and context-awareness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should tailor content and interactions based on learner profile, context of use, and device capabilities to support effective learning experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery, access, evaluation, storage and retrieval of learning objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Support ability to discover, access, evaluate, store, and retrieve learning objects on mobile devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide metadata, searchable catalogs (DRR), persistent links (PURLs), and lightweight packaging of learning objects for mobile discovery and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and evaluation of learning outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms to monitor, utilise, and evaluate learning outcomes delivered via mobile devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include tracking, assessment data capture, and reporting in mLMSs to permit evaluation of effectiveness (e.g., measuring improvements in test scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Error recovery and support during learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist in the recovery of breakdowns and errors during and due to learning activities on mobile devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design robust error messages, offline caching, retry mechanisms, and clear support/help flows to reduce interruption and frustration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for learner mobility (technical and pedagogic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the learner's mobility — both in the technology (connectivity, reformatting) and pedagogy (activities suitable for mobile contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure seamless transitions between contexts (desktop ↔ mobile), synchronize progress, and design micro-tasks for mobile consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple media literacy and multimedia support
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize learners' multiple media literacy and provide multi-format materials (audio, video, enhanced audio with pictures, chaptering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer MP3 audio versions, video clips, enhanced podcasts with chapters and images, and ensure learners can navigate multimedia materials effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate feedback in learning activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instant feedback on learner responses to enhance learning and motivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: mobile ESL exercises give immediate correctness feedback and allow retries. Feedback should be concise and actionable for short mobile interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation and opportunity for continued learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Design to increase learner motivation and encourage continued engagement with mobile content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use incremental successes, progress indicators, and easy access ('one click away') to foster sustained engagement and promote further learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evaluation metrics (pilot-study outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete evaluation metrics such as test score changes, perceived accessibility, perceived quality of learning, willingness to take more mobile lessons, and recommendation rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot results example: slight test-score improvement; 90% agreed on accessibility; 69% felt quality increased; 60% would take more and recommend to friends. Collect both objective and subjective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality measurement challenge: align software and educational purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational value depends on both how an application runs (software) and its underlying educational purpose; difficult to define a unique general instructional standard for m-learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both technical performance and pedagogical design together; be cautious about imposing a single instructional approach across diverse mobile contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content formatting for device and bandwidth (multiple bitrate/format support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide content in formats and bitrates suitable for different devices and bandwidths (e.g., MP3, RealMedia; high-speed and low-speed versions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer streaming and downloadable options; supply compressed audio/video and lower-resolution media to accommodate constrained networks and device capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library and information services integration (mobile catalog features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile integration of library services: search/browse catalogue, check due dates, request materials, and view patron records formatted for device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement server-side reformatting (e.g., AirPac's JSP responses) and device-aware displays; ensure mobile users can perform common library tasks efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management, cost, and infrastructural considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider cost-effective management of m-learning processes, digital rights management (DRM), mLMSs, and necessary technical/professional development investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional investments in infrastructure, professional development, and support systems (physical plant, technical infrastructure) influence recruitment and teaching effectiveness.
